#5277. Core Scientific plans to shut down Bitcoin mining despite Q3 revenue hitting $233M

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Core Scientific, once the largest Bitcoin [BTC] miner, has released its Q3 2026 report, but at the same time it has also announced its plans to completely exit Bitcoin mining by the end of 2026.

During its Q3 2026 earnings call, Chief Financial Officer Jim Nygaard said the company expects to complete the mining wind-down in the fourth quarter and enter 2027 as a high-density colocation provider.

This decision came as the firm’s Q3 results were primarily driven by the expansion of its high-density colocation (HDC) business, which supports AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads.

Remarking on the same, CEO Adam Sullivan said,

We are nearing full delivery under our first colocation agreement while construction under our second is underway across five campuses.

According to the reports, the company’s colocation revenue surged nearly 60% quarter-over-quarter to $215.4 million, compared to $136.7 million in Q2 2026 and $15 million in Q3 2025.

In fact, its total revenue also increased to $232.9 million, up from $164.2 million in the previous quarter and $81.1 million a year earlier.

As of the 30th of September, Core Scientific was billing for 485 megawatts (MW) of capacity, up from 395 MW in the previous quarter, representing more than $700 million in average annualized colocation revenue.

That said, the company also reported net income of $1.178 billion, compared to a net loss of $1.15 billion in Q2 2026 and $144 million in Q3 2025.

Meanwhile, adjusted EBITDA more than tripled quarter-over-quarter to $133.6 million, with its margin expanding to 57% from 25% in the previous quarter. Core Scientific’s gross profit also climbed to $123.3 million, compared to $70 million in Q2.

However, on the mining side, self-mining revenue declined to $12.3 million from $21.5 million in the previous quarter, while hosted mining revenue stood at $5.17 million. At the same time, revenue from hosting equipment for other Bitcoin miners also declined to $5.2 million from $8.7 million.

For those unaware, Core Scientific began its AI infrastructure transition in 2024 through hosting agreements with CoreWeave, covering 590 MW of capacity, of which 485 MW was billable by September 2026. However, the transition also comes with challenges.

Core Scientific recorded $266.5 million in mining-related asset impairments in Q1 2026 amid weaker Bitcoin prices, low mining profitability, and declining equipment values. It also recorded a $41.9 million loss after terminating mining equipment agreements with Block and Proto in Q2.

That said, Core Scientific is not the only one, as, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin miners are increasingly selling BTC to fund operations while shifting their infrastructure towards AI and HPC.

This comes as miners swung from a huge inflow spike of about +7K BTC  in early 2026 to an outflow of about -5.7K BTC in early November, while the price slid from around $95K to $75.5K.

However, the latest netflow has settled back to a small positive reading of about 179.4 BTC, which suggests the miner selling pressure has cooled.

#5276. EIP-8037 state-gas rules force Ethereum dApps to rewrite billing

A Nov. 6 appeal asks projects to test gas assumptions and report repair options that could shape Glamsterdam’s specifications.

Ethereum’s core developers are asking application teams to help decide whether proposed gas changes in the Glamsterdam upgrade need revision, because their own audits cannot cover every project’s contracts and off-chain services.

In a Nov. 6 post on the Ethereum Foundation blog, Marius van der Wijden asked developers and auditors to check eight gas assumptions affected by the proposed upgrade. Security auditors ChainSecurity and Dedaub are investigating alongside internal audits, but the review also needs projects to explain how they could repair affected systems.

The Hoodi testnet’s planned Oct. 26 activation and accompanying 200 million gas-limit increase were postponed on Oct. 22.

The Nov. 6 appeal says the delay continues pending resolution, while the notices leave mainnet activation unset.

The consequences extend from relayers recovering too little of their transaction costs to wallet authorizations becoming reusable after a particular kind of failure. That makes application repairability part of the evidence developers need when weighing changes to the upgrade.

Glamsterdam’s EIP-8037 would raise the cost of creating persistent blockchain data and meter that state growth separately from execution, and EIP-8038 would reprice access and writes to existing state.

The aim is to support higher throughput while controlling the data Ethereum nodes must retain.

The eight-invariant framework separates three price assumptions, covering fixed budgets and reserves, from five accounting assumptions involving gas returns, failure handling, billing and delegation.

A relayer pays to execute a transaction for someone else and may recover that expense by measuring gas before and after the work. The framework’s INV-5 entry explains how the proposed accounting can disrupt that calculation.

Under EIP-8037, a transaction initially funds a separate state-gas reservoir when its gas limit exceeds 16,777,216. State creation draws from that pool first, then execution gas. Solidity’s gasleft() reading excludes the reservoir, so subtracting two readings can miss costs that the relayer actually pays.

If the later reading exceeds the earlier one, checked subtraction reverts, blocking the operation. Unchecked subtraction can wrap into a large number and potentially produce excessive reimbursement, depending on the surrounding arithmetic and payment checks.

Meanwhile, invisible reservoir spending can leave users undercharged and operators covering the shortfall.

The billing guidance suggests agreeing on a user-signed fee using an estimate under the new rules. Where metering remains necessary, clamping the subtraction and capping payment at a signed maximum limits the charge, while reservoir-funded costs remain outside the measurement.

An open specification proposal, PR #12581, would prevent gas readings from increasing. That would address the subtraction problem, but the reservoir’s billing blind spot would remain.

Under the proposed Glamsterdam rules, gasleft() excludes the state-gas reservoir. Select a funding state to see how the balance charged for one cold new-slot write changes.

Illustrative state with at least 97,920 gas in the reservoir at this write. The execution balance pays 12,100 and the reservoir pays 97,920.

Illustrative state with zero reservoir gas at this write. The execution balance pays the complete 110,020 charge, including the state component.

A funded reservoir can pay the state charge outside gasleft(), while an empty reservoir shifts that charge to the execution balance.

Proposed rules checked November 6, 2026. Operation-level charges exclude intrinsic, wrapper and incidental instruction costs. Initial reservoir funding requires a transaction gas limit above 16,777,216, and later refills may also fund it. Intermediate reservoir balances split the state charge between balances.

Uses the proposed charge for one cold zero-to-nonzero storage write. 12,100 execution + 97,920 state = 110,020 total gas. Funding illustrations assume at least 97,920 reservoir gas or zero at that write. The main bar is proportional, rounded to 0.001 SVG units. Connectors are schematic.

Proposed rules checked November 6, 2026. Operation-level charges exclude intrinsic, wrapper and incidental instruction costs. Initial reservoir funding requires a transaction gas limit above 16,777,216, and later refills may also fund it. Intermediate reservoir balances split the state charge between balances.

INV-8 examines EIP-7702 delegation, where an account authorizes delegated contract code. Under the proposed rules, insufficient gas during pre-execution can leave a transaction included in a block while rolling back its delegation and authorization-related update to the account’s sequence number, or nonce.

An exposed authorization that still satisfies its validity checks, including the authorizing account’s nonce, can then be reused. If the delegated contract also has an initializer that lets the first caller choose the owner, an attacker could apply the authorization and initialize ownership in one transaction.

Authorization front-running already existed in public mempools, but here a failed mined transaction can expose a reusable authorization even after private submission.

Delegations already applied before the top-level execution frame remain in place when that later frame fails. A failed receipt requires further checking of the account’s resulting code and nonce.

Suggested wallet safeguards include binding initialization to the account’s signature or self-calls and invalidating exposed authorizations. Charging the worst-case authorization cost upfront has also been suggested as a protocol change and remains unadopted.

Under the proposed schedule, creating a cold storage slot costs 110,020 total gas, versus 22,100 under Osaka. Of that proposed total, 12,100 is execution gas, and 97,920 is state gas, with the reservoir determining which balance funds the latter.

ChainSecurity’s Oct. 13 research shows how changed costs and returned gas can let a contract finish recording an underfunded operation as permanently unsuccessful. If that record removes the retry path, a valid operation can become impossible to repeat.

Revalidated budgets, propagating failures, and preserving retries address different parts of that risk.

The repository asks affected projects whether a setting, upgrade, or migration can fix their problem, and roughly when. Those answers help developers assess how much compatibility work applications can absorb and where specification changes could prevent damage.

Concrete reports of what breaks and how to repair it will inform the next specification discussions.

According to fresh data from RWA Foundation, citing Token Terminal, XRP Ledger (XRPL) remains the number one undisputed leader in the tokenized commodities market. This is based on the distributed asset value in this particular segment of the RWA tokenization market.

Since the beginning of the year the net inflow of money into XRP-focused ledger totalled $2.2 billion. The nearest competitor is Ethereum, which records a positive delta of $1.6 billion year-to-date. Avalanche closes the top 3 with $335.2 million in attracted capital. Other blockchain platforms like BNB Chain, Solana, and Coinbase amassed collectively less than $100 million out of yearly $4.2 billion flow.

Stats from RWA.xyz shed more light on how XRP Ledger's leadership is constructed:

The key driver behind the tokenization breakthrough is JMWH fund by Justoken platform worth $2.23 billion. It represents tokenized contracts on electroenergy generation in Latin America, structured within Argentine and UK legal fields. At the moment there are 172 holders of this on-chain fund.

Apart from this, other tokenized commodities on the XRP Ledger look slightly modest. Generally they are presented with a retail collection of tokenized diamonds from Ctrl Alt with the biggest position estimated at $105 million. The Justoken contract is so massive that it is the biggest real-world asset overall in the XRP-based ecosystem, making the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin and tokenized bonds by Ondo Finance yield to it as well with $896 million and $185 million respectively.

Without Justoken, the XRP Ledger would be just 5th in the segment ranking. Nevertheless, two months are left in 2026, and the blockchain platform continues to headline the tokenized commodities market, making its success one of the most notable industry breakthroughs of the year.

Home » Altcoins » USELESS Jumps 15% as Buyers Enter Sideways Memecoin Market

A satirical meme coin stands out from the heavily-red market with double-digit percentage gains as some buying sentiment returns.

USELESS coin rose 15% after announcing its LONG launch, pulling buyers back into the token while conditions across the broader memecoin market stayed uneven. The move reversed near-term sentiment sharply, yet current signals still do not point to a clear or lasting recovery.

The LONG announcement gave USELESS a clear short-term catalyst and helped lift the price as traders stepped back in. A 15% gain stands out for a smaller, sentiment-driven token, where relatively modest shifts in demand can produce outsized swings, as seen after the midterms.

Useless coins being exposed for what they are. https://t.co/9TMXVejVNU pic.twitter.com/7fKu12menT

This price advance looks driven more by renewed attention around the launch itself than by any confirmed improvement in the wider trading environment. Event-driven moves can attract quick inflows, but they also tend to fade once the initial reaction cools or broader appetite softens.

The recovery faces at least two immediate risks: sellers using the bounce to exit positions, and market conditions that fail to support continued speculative demand. Without steady buying after the initial launch reaction, USELESS could struggle to hold its gains.

$USELESS gave back the rally. a rough day across the board.closed at $0.1266, down 10.0%, alongside BTC −5.5%, S&P −4% and Nasdaq −6%.it held up better than i expected given the selloff. still, yesterday’s test was whether buyers could defend $0.132–$0.134 after reclaiming… pic.twitter.com/T9cKBEiZoH

Memecoin price action depends heavily on momentum, attention, and liquidity. When any of those cools, a token that has risen quickly can also retrace sharply, especially if many buyers entered mainly for the nearest-term USELESS meme coin catalyst.

The 15% rise shows buyers remain willing to respond to new developments. Mixed market conditions, however, leave the meme rebound vulnerable until demand proves more durable.

For now, the LONG launch has brought fresh interest, but the token still needs consistent participation beyond the initial reaction if the move is to develop into something more lasting.

#5273. Strive Reports $509M Quarterly Profit as Bitcoin Buying Accelerates

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Strive reported $509 million in third-quarter GAAP net income and said it purchased 8,136 BTC during the quarter, followed by another 15,124 BTC between October 1 and October 30. Its financing structure and accounting gains matter as much as the headline accumulation figures.

Bitcoin treasury company Strive has released a new set of numbers showing how rapidly its balance sheet has changed. In its November 6 third-quarter results, the Nasdaq-listed business reported $509 million in GAAP net income for the three months to September 30, alongside a large expansion of its Bitcoin position.

Strive said it acquired 8,136 BTC during the quarter and 20,373 BTC over the first nine months of 2026. It then bought another 15,124 BTC from October 1 through October 30. These are company-reported acquisition numbers, not an independent estimate of the market’s available Bitcoin supply.

The company reported $490.4 million in cash and cash equivalents as of October 30, plus a $50.1 million fair-value position in Strategy’s STRC preferred shares. It also closed an offering of seven million SATS preferred shares on October 20, reporting roughly $609 million in net proceeds after underwriting costs.

These details change how investors should interpret the Bitcoin buying. Purchasing more coins is easy to describe. The harder question is how those purchases are financed and how the resulting returns and risks are distributed among common and preferred shareholders. Preferred securities can provide capital, but they also introduce terms and obligations that differ from simply holding Bitcoin in a wallet.

That makes direct comparisons between treasury businesses difficult. NewsBTC recently reported Strategy’s purchase of another 811 BTC, a transaction accompanied by its own capital-management decisions. The underlying asset may be the same, but the capital structures are not.

Strive’s GAAP profit is an accounting figure reflecting the company’s reported results under applicable rules. Bitcoin price changes can create substantial gains or losses in reported earnings without corresponding sales or cash receipts. Investors need to inspect the financial statements and reconciliations rather than assume a nine-figure profit represents operating cash generated from customers.

The company also disclosed a third-quarter Bitcoin yield of 18.5% and a year-to-date yield of 63.2%. Those are management-defined measures intended to assess Bitcoin growth relative to a particular share denominator. They are not conventional investment yields, cash dividends or guaranteed returns. As the share count and preferred capital change, the denominator matters enormously.

Strive said it was evaluating additional balance-sheet strategies spanning lending, brokerages, decentralised finance, reinsurance and tokenisation. Evaluating an opportunity is not the same as launching a product. Each area carries regulatory, counterparty or execution risks that could complicate an otherwise straightforward treasury narrative.

Three things deserve attention: updated fully diluted share counts, the costs and terms of preferred financing, and the company’s actual liquidity alongside its Bitcoin exposure. A rising coin balance is not sufficient evidence that every existing shareholder’s economic interest in those coins has increased.

The company’s November 6 release provides a useful dated snapshot rather than an assurance of future performance. NewsBTC’s reporting on the broader Bitcoin hashrate cycle is a reminder that the coin’s market and infrastructure operate beyond any one corporation’s strategy. For now, Strive has demonstrated aggressive accumulation. Whether it creates durable value for common shareholders will depend on capital discipline as much as on Bitcoin itself.

The current market breakdown could go either way.

On one hand, this can lead to a further capitulation phase for the market as key support levels come under threat. However, it could also be seen as a bear trap for those short sellers who have stretched their positions too far. Notably, XRP seems to be at the forefront of this debate.

As the chart below shows, Bitfinex XRP shorts have spiked by 652.89% to 468.2 million. Given the weakening technical momentum, this bearish positioning is not entirely surprising. The altcoin has seen five straight  weekly lows and broken below the $1.20 support level, with its price now approaching the $1 mark.

Meanwhile, XRP’s relative strength is adding another layer of pressure.

After breaking out of its five-week consolidation, the XRP/ETH pair has dropped over 3% this week. This indicates that XRP is losing value to Ethereum, as traders are showing preference towards ETH in this current bear trend. This relative weakness in XRP is therefore contributing to the bearish sentiment.

From a technical standpoint, betting on more Ripple [XRP] downside, with $1 as the next target, looks like a calculated move rather than a random bet. However, on-chain signals are telling a different story, keeping the possibility of a bear trap on the table.

XRP is flashing textbook signs of a potential supply shock.

On the 5th of September, an estimated 13.24 million XRP was taken off exchanges, limiting the amount available to sell (as noted by one analyst). Moreover, whale holdings have increased by nearly 60 million XRP over the past week. While it is unclear whether these are the same tokens that left exchanges, both signals point to growing accumulation by large holders.

The key takeaway? XRP’s Binance Scarcity Index has hit its highest level since 2022. As shown in the chart below, the index has been deeply negative throughout September and October before making a sharp move higher in recent days. The index is now extremely positive, and it is one of its largest movements in almost 4 years. This indicates that XRP supply is becoming tighter on Binance.

Ultimately, XRP is showing a clear split between its technical and on-chain signals.

While negative momentum and increasing short interest indicate that there is more downside to come, market outflows, whale accumulation, and reduced Binance supply suggest that selling pressure may be losing steam. If these supply patterns remain, then those shorting the market hoping for a fall to $1 may be caught off guard, turning the current bearish setup into a potential bear trap.

Rising XRP shorts and weak price action point to a possible drop toward $1.

Whale buying and exchange outflows suggest supply is tightening, raising the risk of a bear trap.

#5271. Solana Targets Hong Kong's Tokenization Market

Solana Company seeks to broaden its footprint in Hong Kong amid rising interest from major financial institutions in tokenized assets in the Asian financial hub.

As reported by the South China Morning Post on Nov. 6, the Nasdaq-listed firm is seeking to leverage rising demand for blockchain-based financial products as the Asia-Pacific region emerges as one of the major growth opportunities for its business.

Solana Company Chairman and CEO Joseph Chee thinks Asia-Pacific could be one of the most exciting markets for Solana's ecosystem.

The firm already has its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Hong Kong and is positioning itself as a provider of digital asset infrastructure and related services.

Last month, Solana Company was listed as one of Hong Kong's strategic enterprises by the Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises. The designation emphasized the firm's potential role in Hong Kong's burgeoning digital asset sector.

The firm now aims to identify opportunities to offer traditional financial institutions blockchain infrastructure, especially for their work in tokenizing real-world assets.

Hong Kong has been pushing for tokenization as part of its efforts to become a global digital asset hub.

During Hong Kong FinTech Week earlier this week, Securities and Futures Commission CEO Julia Leung announced that regulators had already approved 17 tokenized investment products for retail investors.

In total, the products manage around $1.3 billion in assets (a 34% surge from last year).

Although the tokenization industry has been growing, Chee admitted that Hong Kong is not as advanced as the U.S. when it comes to tokenization.

Even so, the fact that Hong Kong's tokenization industry is still nascent might be an opportunity for firms that could offer the necessary infrastructure.

Solana Company is now looking into boosting its local presence in Hong Kong to leverage the rising demand.

Chee said the firm might be ready to scale up its local workforce from fewer than 10 employees to as many as 30.

The next six months will be crucial for assessing the growth of the local market.

#5270. Millions watched Kalshi’s election odds without betting a dollar

On election night, millions watched Kalshi's probabilities shift in real time, even though most visitors never traded a contract.

Kalshi says people watching its midterm markets outnumbered traders five to one. For those spectators, Kalshi offers a forecast that keeps moving while the country waits for an answer.

You could spend election night on Kalshi without buying anything, as millions of people did this week. Its midterm display offered maps of congressional races and gauges tracking control of the House and Senate, with percentages changing in real time as the evening unfolded.

It's easy to understand why traders keep such a close eye on Kalshi: every little change in odds changes the value of their positions. Given how much money actually moved hands during the midterms, it's no wonder hundreds of thousands of traders were glued to the platforms.

But millions of people were also looking at Kalshi who weren't making any bets, with most not even having accounts on the platform. In October, Kalshi said viewers of its midterm markets outnumbered traders five to one.

Kalshi’s post-election recap reported more than $2.5 billion in midterm trading volume, compared with $1.3 billion for the 2024 election cycle.

Kalshi's Nov. 4, 2026 recap reports $1.3 billion for the 2024 election cycle and more than $2.5 billion for 2026 midterm markets. The 2026 bar marks the reported lower-bound threshold, not an exact total. Kalshi uses notional volume to measure trading activity; these figures do not count viewers or unique traders. The recap does not specify matching market coverage or start and end times for the two periods.

Source: Kalshi: 2026 midterms recap, Nov. 4, 2026 · Kalshi: prediction-market volume convention, footnote 1

While Kalshi's numbers are hard to verify and the company hasn't provided an exact measurement period or a definition of its ratio, they show a second use for the exchange: following politics without placing a bet, while letting the people who do bet help shape your expectations.

On Aug. 20, 2008, Wolf Blitzer turned to CNN's internet reporter, Abbi Tatton, for an update on speculation about Barack Obama's running mate. Tatton brought him a number from Intrade, an online prediction market: Joe Biden was trading at about 36%.

Biden led the other candidates she named and would ultimately get the job, although 36% still left substantially more room for someone else to be chosen.

Tatton also mentioned CNN's own political market, which used virtual dollars. Viewers could follow the odds or play along without risking real money. Everybody wanted to put a number on political suspense, and it was a perfect fit for a television segment about the elections.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Kalshi's election hub combines market odds with polling averages, fundraising figures, and campaign news, giving visitors several ways to follow a race in one place.

A contract paying $1 if a candidate wins, and nothing if they lose, might trade at 65 cents. That price is commonly read as roughly a 65% chance of victory, although fees, available trading volume, and the contract's rules slightly erode those numbers.

Polls gather answers from a sample of people, forecasts estimate an outcome based on historical evidence and assumptions, and a market then sets a price at which participants will trade. These can inform one another, but a percentage alone doesn't reveal how it was produced or what it measures.

The trader has to decide whether 65 cents is worth paying, and the spectator can simply take away the expectation that the candidate will probably win. That means that someone else's financial judgment has become part of their understanding of the election.

The market still has something to show you between a poll's release and the next substantial development. It can adjust after a debate, absorb new returns, or reflect a change in how traders interpret already available evidence.

Those movements look much the same on a screen: a percentage rises or falls, inviting the viewer to read the change as news.

Kalshi acknowledges in its explanation of why prices move that fresh information is only one cause. Trader behavior can also push prices away from a reasonable estimate, and watching the percentage doesn't necessarily reveal what has happened.

A candidate can appear to be gaining ground because the chance attached to their name has increased, even when no additional voter has been interviewed and no additional ballot counted.

An experiment involving 1,994 registered voters showed how easily those percentages can shape expectations.

Participants saw pairs of hypothetical congressional candidates, with randomly varied polling figures and market odds. Higher displayed odds made respondents more likely to identify a candidate as the expected winner.

Traders can bring knowledge that a casual observer lacks, and money gives someone who spots a mistaken price a reason to act. The commercial effort to attract an audience doesn't remove the possibility that the resulting forecast is good.

But a poll and a market reacting to that poll can look like two separate endorsements of a candidate's prospects when they draw on the same evidence. Those just observing the market get more perspectives without necessarily getting more independent information.

In its post-election recap, Kalshi said its markets reached 99% for Democratic House control at 8:10 p.m. Eastern and passed that level for Senate control at 9 p.m.

The company said its prices reflected anticipated results ahead of television networks and offered replays showing how the graphics changed through the evening.

But an exchange and a newsroom have to answer different questions, since a market can express overwhelming confidence while leaving room for a loss.

The Associated Press says it calls a race only when the trailing candidates no longer have a path to victory. For congressional control, it counts the seats actually needed for a majority.

Neither a price nor a news organization's call is the official certification of an election. But the call takes responsibility for saying the outcome has been established, a different claim from assigning it a probability.

A market that gets to 99% first doesn't show that journalists took longer to perform the same task.

AP supplies Kalshi with vote counts and race calls, which the exchange places alongside its forecasts and traders can use to reconsider their positions. The market depends in part on the reporting against which it is judged.

Kalshi's recap points readers toward international elections and the 2028 presidential contest, inviting them to follow the odds beyond one election night.

Spectators will most likely want an early estimate from a prediction market but still wait for a newsroom to declare a winner.

The price of these contracts shows how strongly traders expect an outcome, and the race call says the remaining votes can no longer change it. People who never risk a dollar still have to decide how much authority to give the price, especially when its movement is the only thing that has changed.

#5269. BitFuFu’s October Bitcoin Mining Output Falls Despite Steady Hashrate

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: BitFuFu produced 137 BTC in October, down from 167 in September, while managed hashrate stayed close to 19.5 EH/s. The miner attributed the decline partly to rising network difficulty, illustrating why steady capacity does not necessarily mean steady production.

A Bitcoin miner can run broadly the same amount of computing power and still produce fewer coins. BitFuFu’s latest monthly operating statement provides a neat example. The company reported November 6 that it mined 137 BTC in October, down from 167 in September, even as total hashrate under management remained largely unchanged.

Its managed rate stood at 19.5 exahashes per second, compared with 19.4 EH/s a month earlier. The company held 1,454 BTC at October’s end, up from 1,388 in September. Production decreased while the treasury balance increased, because production and coin retention are separate measures.

BitFuFu said Bitcoin network difficulty rose about 11.8% during October, from 132.76 trillion at the beginning of the month to 148.36 trillion at month-end. Difficulty adjusts how hard it is for miners collectively to find valid blocks. When competition increases, a miner with an unchanged share of computing power may capture a smaller share of the rewards than before.

The split inside BitFuFu’s operation was also revealing. Self-mining production fell to 67 BTC from 98 BTC, while cloud-mining production was nearly flat at 70 BTC against 69 BTC in September. Total monthly production therefore declined by 30 BTC, but the effect was not identical across its operating categories.

NewsBTC recently examined Bitcoin’s recovery above one zettahash of network hashrate. That broader competition can be healthy for network security while making mining economics more demanding for individual operators. It is possible for both statements to be true at once.

BitFuFu’s average fleet efficiency improved to 16.3 joules per terahash from 16.7 in September. Lower energy use per unit of hashing is useful, although it does not automatically offset higher difficulty, power prices, financing costs or changes in Bitcoin’s market price. The company also reported power capacity under management of 317 megawatts, compared with 324 MW a month earlier.

These figures are particularly relevant when evaluating mining businesses that sell both direct Bitcoin exposure and computing services. Managed hashrate can include machines owned by clients or supplied by third parties, not just equipment on the company’s balance sheet. Investors should therefore distinguish self-owned hashrate, contractual capacity, energy efficiency and coins actually received.

A miner accumulating coins can improve its Bitcoin exposure even while production slows. But treasury growth alone says little about the cost of producing each BTC or the cash needed to keep equipment operating. The real test is whether operations remain resilient when difficulty rises and the market price fails to keep pace.

The next report will show whether October’s production weakness was temporary or persisted under the next difficulty environment. Useful metrics include self-mined output, third-party mining contribution, installed and energised capacity, average fleet efficiency and the amount of Bitcoin retained rather than sold.

BitFuFu’s figures are unaudited operating metrics, not a full measure of profitability. They nevertheless make the central point clearly: Bitcoin mining is a competitive process, and an operator can improve its hardware efficiency while producing fewer coins. That is why mining comparisons need more than a headline hashrate number.

Node 11.2 is expected to hit mainnet by 8th November, and it will bring Dijkstra features with it.

Usually, a big release would give the price something to work with. Not this time though.

Cardano Node 11.2 is out… only as a pre-release for now. The GitHub notes say it isn’t recommended for mainnet yet. The full release, likely tagged 11.2.1, is expected by the weekend (8th November).

The biggest change isn’t quite obvious though.

Node configs now come in a new “envelope” format; nodes older than 11.2 won’t be able to read them. Basically, this means operators will have to upgrade. The node’s API also got a boost. It can now run over a network address instead of only locally, and it picked up new tools for checking the mempool.

On the Dijkstra side, the CLI now handles sub-transactions. Dijkstra transactions can be submitted through the API too.

Leios is only groundwork here, and it’s switched off by default. The real thing is planned for Node 11.3, which is already being built.

… a $0.19 liquidity cluster is right above it.

The sell-off involved ADA falling from about $0.199 on 5th November to a low near $0.178 overnight.

The altcoin eventually clawed its way back to $0.186. However, at press time, it was still 6.7% below where it began.

The RSI on the short-term chart was at 48.3 too.

Additionally, the leverage has also taken multiple hits. Open Interest went down from about $197 million to $181 during the drop.

Funding seemed to be positive too with a reading of 0.0057%. This implied that longs haven’t given up yet.

Here’s what’s interesting, though. There appeared to be big pile of liquidations stacked on the heatmap, between $0.188 and $0.19. These seemed to be just above the press time trading price.

Prices cam often drift toward spots like that.

If Cardano pushes into that zone, those shorts could get squeezed… fast.

Gnosis Pay, a fintech project from Britain, officially confirmed that data belonging to holders of its retail Visa debit cards was compromised. The breach which took place on November 3 continues the trend of this fall, when attackers no longer need to go after blockchains or smart contracts. It’s far easier for them to hit the traditional fiat infra that links digital assets to the real world.

Institutional partners and investors can exhale as the company’s enterprise and white-label B2B platform is running normally. For ordinary users, the key point is that the crypto in their wallets is safe, as the company said funds were not affected either. Card issuer Monavate Limited, which is regulated by the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority, continues to operate as well. The hackers walked away with data only.

This time the unauthorized access involved a legacy B2C card processing system. The Gnosis Pay platform was already being prepared for retirement, with a full shutdown scheduled for December 20. According to the official explanation, after the hack happened, Gnosis Pay’s security team moved fast to contain the threat and cut off access via the compromised keys within two hours.

The Gnosis Pay incident rounds out a trilogy of major leaks this fall and exposes a weak spot shared by crypto-fiat gateways. The timeline of the past few weeks points to a clear pattern evident in Ledger, Trezor, SafePal and Keystone leaks throughout 2026.

Gnosis Pay has finished emailing affected users with a detailed list of the exposed data. Until the system goes offline next month, the company is operating in emergency mode with transaction monitoring being upped, and 3D Secure verification is now mandatory for all online payments.

Of course, the company has also issued an urgent phishing alert. Armed with purchase details, addresses and personal data, scammers are already starting to pose as official customer support. The Gnosis Pay team urges users to be suspicious of all incoming requests and reminds them that “we and our Partner Apps will never ask” for security credentials such as seed phrases, private keys, PINs or full card numbers to verify or cancel transactions. Finally, any account changes are legitimate only when users make them directly within the official app.

#5266. Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Testnet Step Over Gas-Accounting Risks

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Ethereum developers have postponed the next Glamsterdam hard-fork step on the Hoodi testnet after researchers identified applications that may depend on gas-accounting assumptions the upgrade would change. The Ethereum Foundation is asking teams to audit code before the process advances.

Ethereum’s next major protocol upgrade has hit an important compatibility check. In a November 6 update, Ethereum Foundation developer Marius van der Wijden said the Glamsterdam testing process would not proceed to the Hoodi fork until problems identified during testing were resolved.

The concern is not that the Ethereum network has stopped functioning. Rather, some existing applications could break because they rely on assumptions about how gas is charged. The Foundation identified EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 as the proposals that require closer scrutiny.

Ethereum gas is commonly understood as the cost of executing transactions and smart-contract operations. Developers also use gas-related properties inside application design and testing. If the protocol alters the accounting model, code built around old assumptions can behave differently even when its business logic has not been edited.

The Foundation said ChainSecurity had found projects that could be vulnerable after Glamsterdam because they depend on invariants that the proposed changes would break. An invariant is a condition developers assume will continue to hold. Breaking one does not automatically mean every affected contract can be exploited, but it can introduce incorrect behaviour, unexpected failures or security exposure.

The engineering team is working with ChainSecurity and Dedaub, alongside internal auditing efforts. It has also published a repository describing eight relevant invariants and examples that developers can check. This is a call for affected application teams to participate in the review, not merely an internal protocol discussion.

Blockchain upgrades have a difficult obligation: improve the underlying platform without unexpectedly damaging applications already deployed on it. The network is open, and its developers cannot inspect every third-party contract, off-chain integration or custom execution path. Testnets and audits are designed to identify precisely this kind of problem before users face it in production.

The Foundation said AllCoreDevs decided not to fork Hoodi until the issues were resolved, while work on the later Hegota upgrade would continue in parallel. That separation is useful. It suggests the immediate bottleneck sits in the Glamsterdam compatibility review rather than a blanket suspension of all Ethereum development.

For operators, the responsible response is practical rather than dramatic. Teams should check whether their contracts or surrounding code depend on the identified gas assumptions, test against the updated specifications and document any affected flows. Even a contract that appears unchanged could be involved if another component makes assumptions about its gas use.

The November 6 post did not establish a new final deployment date, so assigning one would be speculation. The meaningful milestones are revised specifications if necessary, confirmed remediation of affected cases, a successful Hoodi test and clear guidance for applications that may need modifications.

Ethereum’s wider activity continues independently of this testing decision. NewsBTC has recently tracked ETF flows, but fund demand and protocol engineering should not be collapsed into one cause-and-effect story. Here, the verifiable development is a cautious pause after discovering compatibility risk. For a network hosting substantial financial activity, finding that risk before deployment is the critical distinction.

#5265. Morpho loan stress exposes cbXRP, but spares native XRP

A Nov. 6 snapshot placed 8.84 million USDC across 1,070 positions within a further 10% oracle decline, assuming unchanged debt and collateral.

A 10% decline from the collateral price recorded around 13:24 UTC on Nov. 6 would make positions carrying about 8.84 million USDC of debt eligible for liquidation in a Morpho lending market on Base.

The snapshot covered 1,070 positions borrowing USDC against cbXRP, Coinbase's XRP-backed token. A smaller 5% decline would bring 462 of those positions, carrying about 3.23 million USDC of debt, to or beyond the same boundary.

For XRP holders who borrow against their tokens, further price weakness creates a choice between repaying debt, committing more collateral, or facing liquidation. Borrowing preserves exposure to the asset, while adding a financial obligation that becomes harder to support as collateral loses value.

Coinbase describes cbXRP as a wrapped token backed 1:1 by native XRP held in its custody. A holder can use an existing XRP position as collateral, so rising loan balances alone do not create new XRP purchases.

At 13:24 UTC, the market carried about 59.2 million USDC of total debt against roughly 119.9 million cbXRP in collateral. The debt inside the further-10% stress bucket represented approximately 15% of that borrowing, and the affected positions held about 12.73 million cbXRP.

Conditional exposure in one Base cbXRP/USDC market, using November 6 positions with debt and collateral quantities held fixed.

An illustrative 60% starting LTV rises to 66.7% when collateral value falls 10%, leaving debt and collateral quantities unchanged.

At the same lower oracle price, repaying 10% of original debt restores the illustrative position to 60% LTV.

Adding about 11.1% to original collateral quantity at the lower oracle price restores 60% LTV.

The 5% group sits inside the 10% group. Repayments or added collateral can change the outcome.

The market's oracle, the price feed used to value collateral, uses Chainlink's XRP/USD feed with a fixed 1:1 USDC leg, and its reported ratio was about 1.1843 USDC per cbXRP.

Borrower actions can change the exposed balance before prices reach either scenario.

Consider a position starting at 60% LTV. A 10% fall in the oracle price, with debt and collateral quantities unchanged, raises its LTV to about 66.7%, beyond this market's 62.5% threshold.

Repaying 10% of the debt would restore the original 60% LTV at the lower price. Adding about 11.1% to the original collateral quantity would achieve the same result, excluding interest, fees, and further price moves.

The market interface recorded repayments and collateral additions around 13:14-13:16 UTC on Nov. 6. Those transactions show that positions were changing around the observation window.

For borrowers using Coinbase's interface to Morpho on Base, optional automatic collateral protection can add assets after a configured trigger. Borrowers must enable it and have assets available, and volatility or technical problems can prevent execution.

That makes the fixed-position estimate sensitive to both borrower responses and whether intended top-ups actually complete.

Once a position becomes eligible, an external liquidator can repay some or all of its debt and receive collateral plus an incentive. In this market, that exchanges USDC debt repayment for cbXRP collateral.

The exposed positions hold 12.7 million cbXRP, but the amount actually seized depends on subsequent liquidation transactions.

A liquidator may retain or trade that collateral, and any resulting native-XRP sales would require separate evidence linking the liquidation to those sales.

For holders using XRP-backed credit, the immediate pressure is to keep debt supported as collateral values change. Subsequent repayments, collateral additions and executed liquidations will determine how much of this snapshot's exposure remains.

#5264. DarkSword iPhone Exploit Drains $4M in Crypto Theft

Home » Crypto Market News » DarkSword iPhone Exploit Drains $4M in Crypto Theft

Zero-click browser vulnerability drains millions from unpatched devices by targeting stored recovery phrases.

A silent zero-click exploit chain targeting iPhones has drained more than $4 million in cryptocurrency across 365 TRON wallets, according to a report by Bitquery.

Dubbed DarkSword, the sophisticated attack kit compromises unpatched iOS devices through Safari—allowing hackers to extract private keys and seed phrases without requiring a single transaction signature or app download.

DarkSword, a kit for hacking iPhones, chains six iOS vulnerabilities to hijack devices running iOS 18.4 through 18.7. It compromises vulnerable iPhones through malicious websites opened in Apple’s Safari browser.

The exploit chain combines multiple security vulnerabilities to gain access to sensitive device information without requiring users to download an application or authorize a wallet transaction.

Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), together with cybersecurity firms Lookout and iVerify, published technical analyses of the exploit on March 18, 2026. Their findings describe an attack chain capable of accessing passwords, messages, and cryptocurrency wallet information stored in Apple’s Keychain.

A separate investigation by cybersecurity firm Censys identified modules targeting 18 cryptocurrency wallet applications. The toolkit can reportedly search photos and note-taking applications for recovery phrases, potentially exposing wallets whose credentials were stored on the device.

Targeted applications reportedly include MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, and Coinbase. The vulnerability lies in the iPhone’s operating system rather than the individual wallet applications.

Unlike conventional phishing attacks, DarkSword does not necessarily require victims to connect their wallets or approve suspicious transactions. Attackers who obtain a private key or recovery phrase can use another device to sign and broadcast transactions.

Bitquery’s investigation identified a network of 43 collection addresses connected through a shared fee wallet. The addresses received funds from 365 TRON wallets between October 5 and November 4.

The investigation found that at least $4.06 million in USDT was transferred. Of the 365 wallets affected, the median loss was $1,029. Eight wallets lost more than $100,000 each, accounting for 63% of the total USDT losses. The attackers reportedly sent small amounts of TRX to victims’ wallets shortly before draining their balances.

Bitquery traced the transfers back to an initial transaction whose amount and timing matched those of a publicly reported iPhone theft. However, blockchain records cannot reveal which devices or wallet applications individual victims were using.

Apple has released security updates addressing the vulnerabilities used by DarkSword. Google recommends installing the latest available iOS version or enabling Apple’s Lockdown Mode when an update is not possible.

Changing wallet passwords or revoking token approvals is not sufficient if attackers already possess the recovery phrase. A compromised seed requires generating a new one and transferring the assets.

DarkSword device-level attacks bypass wallet approval checks, so exposed seed phrases can lead to total loss without a single signature from the victim.

#5263. Crypto Slump Could Be Far From Over, Barclays Analyst Warns

Another sell-off could be on the way for crypto after a leading strategist at Barclays warned that the recent U.S. stock market rally may not last.

There are more signs of trouble in the cryptocurrency market, with a leading strategist at Barclays warning that the recent rebound in U.S. stocks may not last.

Alexander Altmann, the global head of equities tactical strategies at Barclays, is now somewhat skeptical of the strength of the stock market rebound after the brutal sell-off that has also dragged cryptocurrencies lower.

He lists factors such as negative market breadth, mediocre growth stock performance, a modest rebound in neocloud stocks, the ongoing crypto slump, and a flat quality factor.

The concerns from Altmann come amid increasing worries that the AI investment frenzy that has been a key driver of U.S. equity market performance may not be sustainable.

Barclays strategist was one of the few Wall Street experts who questioned whether the U.S. midterm elections would bring lasting benefits to stocks.

Barclays has flagged the risk that investment strategies sensitive to volatility could help worsen the market decline.

According to Barclays models cited in Bloomberg’s report, volatility-control funds may be at risk of dumping as much as $135 billion of U.S. equity futures in the 24 to 48 hours following Thursday’s market mayhem.

On the Oct. 29 episode of Bloomberg’s Odd Lots podcast, Altmann also argued that investors are in a “denial phase” concerning the risks to the AI sector.

He pointed to growing financing pressure on neocloud companies that host computing resources for AI applications as a sign of early stress in the industry.

Bitcoin [BTC] traders faced liquidations on both sides as prices surged and then erased the rally.

On the 4th of November, Bitcoin climbed from $75.7k to $81.2k, triggering $407.92 million in liquidations. Shorts accounted for $309.98 million of that total.

The reversal on the 5th of November brought another $323.54 million in liquidations, including $294.11 million in longs. Meanwhile, total crypto Market Capitalization fell $132.7 billion that day, bringing losses since the local peak to $149 billion.

Short-term bullish sentiment following the midterm election results was immediately overrun by an equities market pullback, with major AI stocks coming under selling pressure.

In a post on X, Glassnode observed that crypto traders are still here, despite the past month’s price retrace from $87k. Bitcoin [BTC] volume was at its lowest since 2023, before the August rally from $60k commenced.

Thereafter, volume remained above the August levels, which underlined sustained interest from traders and investors.

Rather than being a market collapse, the recent sell-off might be part of a healthy correction. Crypto intelligence platform Santiment posted that the crypto crowd became optimistic following the election results on the 4th of November.

This was a surprise, evidenced by the amount of short liquidations. Fueled by liquidations and FOMO, BTC briefly climbed past $81k.

Short-term FUD in reaction to selling in traditional markets across the globe sparked the Bitcoin reset. In both instances, the price went against the crowd’s expectations, showing why retail trader sentiment extremes can be counter-signals.

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. wrote that the short liquidations reached the highest levels since late September. The Binance heist has also severely affected sentiment.

Since July, short-term holder BTC supply has expanded by 600k. It highlighted coins changing hands from long-term investors to newer market participants, and can also signal increased sensitivity to short-term price trends.

The True Market Mean was at $77.6k, and the brief foray above this level did not last. The metric measures the average cost basis of active investors while filtering out lost, dormant, or long-inactive coins.

A price slip below the TMM implied cooling market conditions and left investors at a loss on average. It could be a warning sign of a deeper correction.

#5261. Samsung Wallet’s USDC on Solana Is Live — Here’s What the Rollout Actually Covers

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

TL;DR: A Solana Foundation update dated November 5 confirms that Samsung Wallet’s stablecoin account went live on November 2 for eligible US Galaxy owners. USDC transfers and certain international bank payouts are supported, but the headline 82 million compatible devices should not be mistaken for 82 million active users.

A crypto feature that does not feel like a crypto feature may be one of the most consequential ways digital payments reach a wider audience. In a November 5 launch confirmation, the Solana Foundation said Samsung Wallet’s Stablecoin Account became available on November 2. For eligible US Galaxy users, it places USDC inside a familiar wallet app rather than asking them to install and learn a separate cryptocurrency application.

That is a tangible step beyond the launch window described in NewsBTC’s earlier look at Samsung’s planned rollout. But the most useful questions concern what people can do today, who qualifies and what still depends on outside providers.

The Foundation says eligible users can buy, hold, send and receive USDC over Solana within Samsung Wallet. Bastion provides licensed custody and infrastructure, with Coinbase serving as sub-custodian through Coinbase Prime Vault. That structure matters. Customers see the convenience of a familiar interface, while their assets still depend on a chain of infrastructure and custody providers.

US customers can transfer USDC to other eligible Samsung Wallet users and compatible external wallets. The announcement says Samsung charges no transfer fee for these routes, although other providers may charge fees. A separate path allows eligible users to send funds to qualifying bank accounts in more than 60 countries, potentially arriving as local currency. Available corridors and charges vary by destination; the distinction between a blockchain transfer and a bank payout is important.

The feature sits inside Samsung Wallet’s Quick access area alongside payment cards and everyday credentials. That small interface decision could matter more to adoption than a headline transaction-speed benchmark, because habitual use often depends on how much friction an app removes.

The announcement refers to approximately 82 million compatible Galaxy devices in the United States. That is a ceiling for potential access, not evidence of adoption. It says nothing about the number of activated accounts, transfers completed, average transaction size or users who return the following month.

The eligibility restrictions are also substantial. According to the Foundation, users need to be at least 18, reside in the US, have a Samsung account and use a compatible Galaxy device running Android 13 or later. New York residents are excluded at launch. These requirements make the real reachable population smaller than the device figure.

The payments story extends the institutional work covered in NewsBTC’s report on Solana’s delivery-versus-payment tool, but the two solve different problems. One targets consumer remittances; the other aims at financial-asset settlement.

Samsung has described potential future expansion into online and in-store stablecoin payments and additional markets, subject to regulation. Those ideas are not live features simply because the stablecoin account has launched. Nor should this launch be read as a forecast for SOL’s price: consumer payments can be valuable without creating a predictable relationship between wallet activity and demand for the network token.

A fair assessment will require active-account numbers, real-world fees, payout times, failed-payment handling and whether the feature reduces friction relative to existing remittance services. The verified news is that the service is now operational for a defined group of customers. The commercial test begins after that announcement, when people decide whether to use it again.

#5260. Stablecoin contraction forces Bitcoin drop despite Fed reserve gains

The dated comparison pairs a reserve rebound with shrinking dollar-token circulation, leaving the link to Bitcoin buying unestablished.

Bank reserve balances rose $67.5 billion between Oct. 28 and Nov. 4, according to the Federal Reserve’s Nov. 5 release, but the more abundant dollar liquidity is not automatically bullish for Bitcoin.

Over the same period, data provider DefiLlama tracked dollar-pegged stablecoin circulation falling by more than 5.7 billion units, or 1.91%.

The split leaves an incomplete picture for a Bitcoin recovery. Higher bank reserve balances would still need to translate into financing and purchases, so the measured token contraction adds a crypto-side observation to that test.

A Nov. 5 Treasury-cash analysis considered a possible December funding window using projected cash paths and the older Oct. 28 reserve baseline. The new release updates that starting point with a rebound in realized reserves.

Coinbase's completed Nov. 5 daily BTC-USD candle closed at $75,969.06, down 5.54% from $80,428.31 on Nov. 4. That close-to-close fall followed the dated reserve observation, putting the price move outside the bank-balance comparison window.

The Fed’s H.4.1 release puts Nov. 4 reserve balances at $2.96 trillion. Over the preceding week, the Treasury General Account, the government’s account at the Fed, fell $79.4 billion to $936.2 billion.

Treasury payments move balances into depository institutions’ accounts, increasing reserves all else equal, while receipts flowing into Treasury’s account work in the opposite direction.

The final reserve change also incorporates movements elsewhere on the Fed’s balance sheet. Total assets rose $2.5 billion, while other balance-sheet changes offset part of the effect of the Treasury-account drawdown.

Tether’s USDT series fell 3.65 billion units, accounting for 63.37% of that measured contraction, while USD Coin (USDC) circulation declined 383 million units, contributing 6.64%. Other tracked dollar-pegged tokens together contracted a net 1.73 billion units.

The issuer breakdown locates the largest measured change in USDT. Whether, and to what extent, issuer redemptions, bridge-accounting adjustments, reclassification, or coverage revisions contributed remains unquantified.

For a liquidity-led recovery thesis, further evidence needs to connect reserve balances with financing and buying. A broader token supply could add evidence about crypto-native dollar availability, while proof of Bitcoin demand would still require its own observations.

Neither supply series resolves the cause of the subsequent selloff, and delayed liquidity effects remain possible. The observed divergence leaves the bank-to-Bitcoin demand channel open.

The cryptocurrency market remains under pressure, as most larger altcoins have corrected: large caps lost around 5% on average in the last 24 hours. Key levels have not been broken yet, but the overall trend is still bearish, despite yesterday's recovery.

From a technical standpoint, XRP has moved further into a downtrend, driven by more liquidations of long positions. According to the Nov. 5 snapshot, more than $12 million worth of longs has been liquidated. While the number itself is not critical, the long liquidations suggest that the asset saw an influx of buying, but it was quickly shut down.

The XRP Ledger activated the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment on November 4 at 14:52 UTC. It removed an exploit that, under certain conditions, let accounts authorized to burn an issuer's tokens also mint them. The native supply of XRP has not been affected, luckily, so illicit actors have not used the exploit.

According to the technical analysis, the price is struggling to hold the important psychological threshold: $1.2 has already been broken, and XRP now trades at approximately $1.2.

The volume influx on the move toward the 21 EMA suggested a possible improvement in market conditions, but low volume on Friday, during the transition into the weekend trading session, disrupted any bullish plans.

As for the future, XRP is clearly moving in a longer-term downtrend; however, we will most likely see a local bounce toward $1.25. An EMA cross between the 100 EMA and the 50 EMA would simply be a signal of further price weakness and trend acceleration (most likely down).

The XRP Ledger has seen substantial growth in various on-chain metrics, which, unfortunately, does not give the price enough support. A lot of the Ledger activity appears to be automated, either trading bots or sophisticated LLM models. The market is mostly driven by speculative interest rather than fundamental network usage.

Hyperliquid fell by almost 9% on Nov. 5 and is now trading below $80, balancing on the 100 EMA, which has been broken temporarily. From a fundamental standpoint, Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) disclosed that it has applied to become a U.S. futures commission merchant. If approved, it would be able to bring U.S. clients directly to the perpetual markets deployed on Hyperliquid.

In addition to this substantial regulatory milestone, Hyperliquid reported $620 million in quarterly net income, including $803 million in unrealized HYPE gains. Before that, on Oct. 29, Hyperliquid announced a separate ICE-Trade agreement; more details are available on the SEC's official website.

From a technical standpoint, on the daily HYPE/USDT chart, the price has bounced somewhat from a local psychological support level of approximately $77. It has been a recovery point for Hyperliquid, but, unfortunately, it is unlikely to hold if more selling pressure appears.

RSI, as a momentum indicator, is moving toward the 40 zone, so any surge of bearish pressure here could be short-lived if it is mostly speculative. However, with volume rising during the descending local trend, the bearish trend is being reinforced.

Hyperliquid (HYPE) lost its pace by the end of September, and a lower high formed in the first days of October, which is essentially the market's main signal of the end of the rally. Despite the spike at the beginning of November, it is still a lower high, which means the bearish trend is not going anywhere.

This is a relatively hard prediction to make, considering the unpredictable nature of the market. Unfortunately, the price has barely any support left, and the next support is the 200 EMA (black line on the chart), which coincides with the $68 price level.

Volume, on the other hand, is falling, which is either a normal tendency before the weekend trading session or a sign of a weakening trend for now.

Key price levels for HYPE are: $80 as the closest psychological support level, $68 as the 200 EMA, and $89 as the first psychological resistance level. The trendline resistance is at approximately $84, so a breakthrough there should become a foundation for a price recovery.

After Stellar (XLM) fell toward $0.157, there is a good chance that we are seeing accumulation or at least a transition into a sideways trend. The moving averages are not converging, which signals trend acceleration, and in this case it is a bearish one. Whenever moving averages converge, volatility is more likely to spike.

The trend on Stellar is accelerating, while volume remains relatively low and neutral.

It is no coincidence that XLM saw a trend slowdown at approximately $0.15, as it coincides with the point where the previous trend started. The death cross that occurred at the end of October is also a bearish signal.

It was followed by a spike in trading volume, which confirms the significance of the indicator and suggests that the trend may continue.

The latest network milestone for XLM is the release of Bell (Protocol 30), which was set to go live on testnet on November 3. The key change it brought to the network was post-quantum signature verification for smart contracts and millisecond ledger timestamps.

However, the mainnet validator vote, which will make the update available to users on the live network, is set to take place on November 23 at 17:00 UTC.

The bearish price performance on the market was followed by a recorded 500,000 XLM long liquidation. But considering the sheer volume of XLM on exchanges, a sub-1 million liquidation barely affects the price and will most likely have a very minor effect on the market.

From the momentum standpoint, RSI is already at a local bottom, and a further drop is possible, despite RSI already sliding to around 30. An oversold RSI is not really an issue when there is profitable capital present.

Considering the behavior of the market, there is a good chance that most of the buying support was at 1.5-1.6, so a break below the $1.5 support level could trigger a further decline, with a possible acceleration toward $1, though this is unlikely and possible only in a very bearish market.

#5258. Same Price, Different Stellar: 69% Growth Outruns XLM On a Red-Day

Home » Altcoins » Same Price, Different Stellar: 69% Growth Outruns XLM On a Red-Day

Stellar continues to add regulated issuers, infrastructure partners, and measurable on-chain volume.

Stellar keeps stacking real-world asset activity and on-chain usage even as its token trades near multi-month lows.

On a day when the broader crypto market shed roughly $120 billion and XLM dropped about 9%, the network still ranked first among tracked chains in tokenized fund growth, adding $291 million.

The $291 million single-day print was not an isolated event.

Over the past ten days the network has added several institutional markers: Janus Henderson launched the first Nasdaq-licensed tokenized fund on Stellar, DTCC went live with Stellar as the first public chain in its setup.

Stellar DEX volume jumped 69% in a week, and almost all of it came from a single protocol.Aquarius, the liquidity protocol on @StellarOrg ($XLM), drove nearly the entire increase, per DeFiLlama.The data ⬇️The full story: https://t.co/ZuB0XcyCRC pic.twitter.com/AZKWxDxcrm

MetaMask began giving every account a Stellar address, Securitize signaled plans to expand, Bell went live on testnet, and Franklin Templeton’s presence on the network reached $1.1 billion.

These moves sit on top of longer-term figures. Stellar has repeatedly led or ranked near the top in tokenized fund inflows across 24-hour, 90-day, and year-to-date windows, even while XLM itself has lagged the network’s asset growth.

Separately, Stellar’s decentralized exchange volume rose 69% over the past week. Nearly the entire increase came from Aquarius, the network’s leading liquidity management protocol, according to DeFiLlama data.

Aquarius has been the dominant DEX by both volume and transactions for some time. Its 30-day volume recently sat near $95 million with cumulative volume above $800 million, and it has held the top spot by total value locked among Stellar DEXs.

🚨 BOOM: Crypto lost $120 billion yesterday. $XLM fell 9%.Same day, #Stellar ranked #1 of all tracked chains in tokenized fund growth: +$291 million.The last 10 days on Stellar:Janus Henderson launched the first Nasdaq-licensed tokenized fund.DTCC went live, with Stellar… pic.twitter.com/zgT0u6tW4C

The rest of the chain’s DeFi activity remains concentrated as well: a handful of protocols account for most of the locked value and trading.

The volume jump is real, yet total value locked on Aquarius has stayed relatively flat even during stronger trading months. That pattern suggests more activity is flowing through existing pools rather than a broad influx of new capital.

XLM is trading back near levels seen before some of the recent institutional announcements.

The gap between network metrics and token price has drawn direct questions from observers: who is required to buy more XLM as tokenized assets and DEX volume grow, and what mechanism turns that activity into sustained demand for the native token?

So far, Stellar’s progress in regulated funds and concentrated DeFi has not produced a matching lift in XLM.

Institutional products on the network often settle in other assets, and much of the on-chain trading runs through a small set of protocols whose fees and incentives do not automatically translate into broad XLM buying.

#5257. Solana’s October Upgrade Review Puts 200ms Slots and $5B in Tokenized Assets in Focus

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Solana Foundation’s November 6 ecosystem review says two protocol changes went live in October: a reduction in target slot time to 200 milliseconds and Alpenglow consensus activation. It also reports a record $5 billion in real-world asset value. These are different metrics, and none alone proves a better experience for every application.

After a month filled with announcements, Solana has published a consolidated account of what changed on its network. The Foundation’s October 2026 ecosystem roundup, released November 6, links a pair of major performance upgrades with increased tokenized-asset activity and a growing roster of payment integrations.

The review is useful because it separates infrastructure that has activated from applications and partnerships still seeking wider use. It also offers a chance to examine how technical speed claims translate into financial operations.

According to the Foundation, a final stage of SIMD-0525 activated on October 9, reducing target slot times from the original 400 milliseconds to 200 milliseconds. Shorter slots aim to reduce the interval at which network leaders produce blocks. They do not guarantee that every transaction is confirmed within 200 milliseconds under all network conditions.

A second change followed on October 21 when Alpenglow replaced TowerBFT consensus on mainnet. The protocol targets roughly 150-millisecond finality. Finality describes when a transaction is sufficiently settled according to the network’s rules, and should not be confused with transaction submission, application response time or a merchant receiving funds in a bank account.

NewsBTC covered the Alpenglow activation earlier in the autumn. The new roundup does not make it a second launch. It provides a broader, dated view of how the two changes fit together, while reminding readers that production reliability has to be measured over time.

The Foundation reports that real-world assets on Solana reached $5 billion in value during October, alongside approximately $60 billion in decentralized-exchange trading volume and 14 million addresses holding stablecoins. These numbers measure different things. Asset value is not trading volume; a blockchain address is not necessarily a person; and gross turnover is not revenue to applications or validators.

The review includes new or expanded connections to traditional finance. J.P. Morgan Asset Management brought tokenized money market funds to the network through Morgan Money. The Foundation also describes stock-related products from Securitize and investment portfolios from Ondo, subject to their own eligibility conditions. For institutional users, the question is not only whether a token can move quickly but whether its legal ownership, redemption rights and custody arrangements remain clear.

That is also the theme behind Solana’s delivery-versus-payment programme, which seeks to coordinate an asset and its payment in one settlement process. Better throughput can help, but it cannot replace legal and operational safeguards.

The Foundation’s update lists stablecoin and remittance activity involving Samsung Wallet, Fiserv and Western Union, as well as integrations with business-payment services. Some products have launched, while other announcements refer to planned support, geographically limited access or commercial pilots. Those distinctions should survive any headline about ‘mainstream adoption’.

For developers and validators, the next meaningful evidence is sustained uptime, consistent finality under load, integration reliability and the cost of operating infrastructure. For investors, it is whether tokenized value corresponds to assets customers can actually redeem and use. Solana’s October was busy by the Foundation’s account; November’s challenge is showing the upgrades make routine financial activity more dependable, not merely more impressive on paper.

#5256. Is crypto’s 2026 outlook at risk as regulatory FUD returns to Washington?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

After the election, investors are looking for clues about crypto’s regulatory future.

However, one thing is clear: the road ahead remains uncertain, with volatility already creeping into the market. The impact of the recent election goes beyond the broader U.S. macro environment, extending into the regulatory landscape as well. The crypto industry has seen huge gains under Republican leadership in the U.S. with President Donald Trump’s vision of making the country the “crypto capital of the world.”

However, with Republicans holding a narrow majority in Congress, investors are becoming more cautious about what comes next. The recent challenges faced with the CLARITY Act, and the increased focus from the SEC around tokenizations, are adding to the uncertainty in the regulatory outlook.

That said, signs of a regulatory shift are already starting to emerge.

In the latest development, House Democrats are drafting a new bill regarding how crypto should be structured moving forward. The bill includes expanding the SEC’s jurisdiction and will also include provisions excluded from the CLARITY Act. This comes ahead of any potential change in who controls Congress.

From a regulatory standpoint, tighter SEC oversight could mean stricter compliance rules, increased scrutiny of crypto firms, and greater regulatory pressure on digital asset companies operating in the U.S. The key takeaway? Regulatory pressure may not stop at tighter SEC oversight.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, known to be a strong crypto critic, is expected to become the Chair of the Senate Banking Committee, potentially giving her greater influence over financial regulation and crypto policy.

Is regulatory FUD shaping up to be the next major bearish catalyst for the broader crypto market?

The recent political upheaval in the U.S. Congress has already started to affect regulation. Discussions around a new crypto market structure bill, increasing anti-crypto sentiment and potential increased scrutiny from the SEC are adding a new layer of uncertainty to an already volatile market.

Further adding to the concern, Bitcoin [BTC] is looking bleak on its yearly chart. Historically, Bitcoin has never closed consecutive years in the red. However, this could change soon.
